headline: FROM TANZANIAN IRON ORE TO HIGH-QUALITY STEEL BILLETS
introduction: Chalinze Steel Mills Ltd is developing an integrated steel manufacturing platform designed to transform Tanzania's Run-of-Mine iron ore into high-quality steel billets through mineral beneficiation, ironmaking, advanced steelmaking and continuous casting.
valueStatement: The integrated production model connects mineral resources with modern industrial manufacturing, with the intention of creating a domestic source of steelmaking feedstock for downstream industries.

stages.title: ROM IRON ORE MINING & EXTRACTION
stages.status: Planned input · mine and supply details require confirmation
stages.description: The integrated steel manufacturing journey begins with Run-of-Mine (ROM) iron ore obtained from identified mineral resources before processing and upgrading. This stage establishes the raw-material foundation for the proposed beneficiation and steelmaking processes. The available company information does not verify operating mine ownership, permits, reserves, supply agreements, or current extraction.

stages.machinery: Mining, material-handling and crushing-feed systems are conceptual; mine fleet and equipment selection are not confirmed.

stages.title: IRON ORE BENEFICIATION & FEED PREPARATION
stages.description: Following extraction, ROM iron ore is planned to undergo beneficiation and feed preparation to improve its suitability for steel manufacturing. Conceptually, valuable iron-bearing material is separated from unwanted mineral fractions and conditioned as a more consistent feedstock. The final process design remains subject to approved engineering.
stages.output: Prepared iron-bearing feedstock (product form and specification to confirm)
stages.machinery: Crushing, screening, grinding, separation, conveying and storage are illustrative process categories only; final equipment selection is not confirmed.
stages.technical: No ore grade, concentrate specification, recovery rate, process yield, water balance or equipment duty is asserted.

hotspots.label: Size reduction
hotspots.detail: Crushing and screening are illustrative beneficiation operations; installed equipment and sizing strategy have not been confirmed.

hotspots.label: Mineral separation
hotspots.detail: Separation illustrates the principle of upgrading iron-bearing material. No specific technology, recovery or concentrate grade is claimed.

stages.title: IRONMAKING — CONVERSION INTO METALLIC IRON
stages.description: Prepared iron feedstock enters the proposed ironmaking stage, where oxygen is removed from iron oxides to create metallic iron for steelmaking. The source material refers both to natural-gas-based Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) and to electric ironmaking configurations. The visualization therefore shows a neutral, conceptual ironmaking stage rather than selecting either route.
stages.input: Prepared iron-bearing feedstock; process route and reductant to confirm
stages.machinery: The reduction vessel, gas systems, electric systems, material handling and plant arrangement are not selected or represented as a final equipment design.
stages.technical: Route conflict requiring company decision: the main narrative describes natural-gas DRI; an alternate diagram describes electric ironmaking. Final approved project engineering must determine the technology.

hotspots.label: Process route
hotspots.detail: Natural-gas DRI and electric ironmaking are both referenced in source material. Neither is selected by this conceptual scene.

hotspots.label: Reduction
hotspots.detail: Reduction represents oxygen removal from iron oxides in principle; process chemistry, equipment and reductant depend on the approved route.

stages.title: STEELMAKING — PRODUCING MOLTEN STEEL
stages.description: Metallic iron is planned to be melted and refined into liquid steel. Steelmaking aims to control chemical composition, temperature, cleanliness and metallurgical characteristics for continuous casting. The company document discusses Electric Arc Furnace steelmaking as a proposed concept; selection, configuration and operating status require approved engineering confirmation.
stages.input: Metallic iron units and approved process additions (details to confirm)
stages.machinery: The conceptual vessel does not establish furnace selection, capacity, supplier, refractory design, ladle configuration, crane arrangement or installed equipment.
stages.technical: No steel chemistry, temperature, cycle time, yield, grade, furnace specification or production capacity is supplied.

hotspots.label: Melting & refining
hotspots.detail: Melting and refining describe process objectives; equipment, charge mix and operating parameters remain subject to approved design.

hotspots.label: Chemistry control
hotspots.detail: Steel composition must be defined by an approved product specification. No grade or composition is represented here.

stages.title: CONTINUOUS CASTING OF STEEL BILLETS
stages.status: Planned process · product dimensions to confirm
stages.description: Molten steel is planned to pass through a continuous-casting system, where controlled cooling transforms liquid steel into solid billet sections. Casting, cooling and process monitoring are intended to support consistent billet formation. Machine design, casting speed and final product tolerances have not been supplied.
stages.machinery: Ladle transfer, moulds, casting equipment, cooling infrastructure, rollers and handling are conceptual categories; no as-built plant configuration is depicted.
stages.technical: The company document lists nominal cross-sections of 130 × 130 mm and 150 × 150 mm; confirm against the final engineering and product specification before publication.
